title: Herbs & Spices Encyclopedia
description: Real culinary herbs and spices with a photo, description, common uses, and substitution alternatives -- pictures are resolved live from Wikipedia the same way museum objects and recipes are.

items.name: Basil
items.description: A sweet, slightly peppery herb central to Italian and Southeast Asian cooking, with many varieties including sweet basil, Thai basil, and holy basil.

items.name: Oregano
items.description: A pungent, earthy herb central to Italian, Greek, and Mexican cooking, more potent dried than fresh.

items.name: Thyme
items.description: A woody, earthy herb used across French, Mediterranean, and Middle Eastern cooking, standing up well to long cooking.

items.name: Rosemary
items.description: A pine-scented, robust herb from the Mediterranean, strong enough to stand up to roasting and grilling.

items.name: Cilantro (Coriander Leaf)
items.description: A bright, citrusy leafy herb essential across Mexican, Indian, Southeast Asian, and Middle Eastern cooking; a genetic taste variation makes some people perceive it as soapy.

items.name: Parsley
items.description: A fresh, mild herb used across European and Middle Eastern cooking, both as a flavouring and a garnish.

items.name: Mint
items.description: A cooling, sweet herb used widely across Middle Eastern, South Asian, and Southeast Asian cuisines.

items.name: Dill
items.description: A feathery, slightly anise-like herb central to Scandinavian, Eastern European, and Russian cooking.

items.name: Sage
items.description: An earthy, slightly peppery herb that pairs strongly with rich, fatty foods.

items.name: Bay Leaf
items.description: A subtly bitter, aromatic leaf used whole in slow-cooked dishes and removed before serving.
alternatives: A small pinch of thyme and oregano combined

items.name: Tarragon
items.description: An anise-scented herb central to classic French cooking.
alternatives: A small amount of fennel or anise seed

items.name: Cumin
items.description: A warm, earthy spice, whole or ground, essential across Indian, Middle Eastern, and Latin American cooking.
alternatives: Ground coriander + a pinch of chilli powder

items.name: Coriander Seed
items.description: The dried seed of the coriander plant, citrusy and slightly sweet, distinct in flavour from the fresh leaf.

items.name: Turmeric
items.description: An earthy, bitter, golden-yellow spice central to South Asian and Southeast Asian cooking, prized for its colour as much as its flavour.
alternatives: Ground ginger + a pinch of saffron for colour (different flavour)

items.name: Paprika
items.description: Ground dried red peppers, ranging from sweet to smoked to hot, central to Hungarian and Spanish cooking.

items.name: Cinnamon
items.description: A warm, sweet bark spice used in both sweet and savoury dishes worldwide.

items.name: Cardamom
items.description: An intensely aromatic, citrusy-floral spice used across Indian, Middle Eastern, and Scandinavian cooking.
alternatives: A mix of cinnamon and nutmeg (different but workable)

items.name: Cloves
items.description: A strong, sweet-pungent spice used sparingly across many world cuisines.

items.name: Nutmeg
items.description: A warm, slightly sweet spice, best freshly grated, used in both sweet and savoury dishes.

items.name: Star Anise
items.description: A star-shaped pod with a strong licorice flavour, central to Chinese and Vietnamese cooking.
alternatives: Fennel seed + a pinch of ground anise

items.name: Fennel Seed
items.description: A sweet, anise-like seed used across Italian, Indian, and Middle Eastern cooking.

items.name: Black Pepper
items.description: The world's most widely traded spice, pungent and sharp, best used freshly ground.

items.name: Cayenne Pepper
items.description: A hot, ground chilli pepper used to add heat across many cuisines.
alternatives: A small amount of chilli flakes or hot paprika

items.name: Saffron
items.description: The dried stigmas of a crocus flower, the world's most expensive spice by weight, prized for its colour and floral-earthy flavour.
alternatives: Turmeric (for colour only, very different flavour)

items.name: Ginger
items.description: A pungent, warming rhizome used fresh, dried, or ground across Asian, Caribbean, and baking traditions.

items.name: Garlic
items.description: A pungent allium used as a foundational aromatic in the vast majority of the world's savoury cuisines.

items.name: Sumac
items.description: A tangy, citrusy ground red spice from dried sumac berries, central to Levantine and Turkish cooking.

items.name: Za'atar
items.description: A Levantine spice blend of dried thyme, sumac, sesame seeds, and salt.
uses: Sprinkled over labneh and olive oil
alternatives: A mix of dried thyme, sesame seeds, and a squeeze of lemon

items.name: Five-Spice Powder
items.description: A Chinese spice blend typically combining star anise, cloves, cinnamon, Sichuan pepper, and fennel seed.
alternatives: A pinch each of cinnamon, cloves, and star anise

items.name: Garam Masala
items.description: A warming North Indian spice blend, typically including cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, cumin, and black pepper.

items.name: Curry Powder
items.description: A British colonial-era invention approximating South Asian spice blends, typically including turmeric, coriander, cumin, and chilli.

items.name: Vanilla
items.description: The cured seed pod of an orchid, one of the most labour-intensive spices to produce, prized for its sweet, floral flavour.
alternatives: Vanilla extract (concentrated, use less than pod scrapings)

items.name: Allspice
items.description: A single dried berry that tastes like a combination of cinnamon, clove, and nutmeg -- despite the name, it is one spice, not a blend.
alternatives: Equal parts cinnamon, clove, and nutmeg

items.name: Mustard Seed
items.description: A pungent seed used whole or ground, central to Indian tempering and Western prepared mustards.

items.name: Fenugreek
items.description: A slightly bitter, maple-like seed and leaf used across Indian, Persian, and Ethiopian cooking.
alternatives: A small pinch of celery seed (different but workable in a pinch)

items.name: Lemongrass
items.description: A citrusy, fibrous stalk essential to Thai, Vietnamese, and other Southeast Asian cooking.

items.name: Galangal
items.description: A peppery, pine-like relative of ginger, essential to Thai and Indonesian cooking.
alternatives: Fresh ginger (different flavour profile, but workable)

items.name: Kaffir Lime Leaf
items.description: An intensely fragrant citrus leaf used whole or shredded in Thai and Southeast Asian cooking.
alternatives: Lime zest (less aromatic, but a reasonable stand-in)

items.name: Chives
items.description: A mild, oniony herb used fresh as a garnish across many cuisines.
